 Appearance:
 Shri Sanjay Sharma - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Pradeep Gupta - G.A. for the respondent/State.
 Order

This is the first application under Section 483 of B.N.S.S. for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.86/2023 registered at Police Station KIrnapur, District Balaghat (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 21(1), 21(2) & 21(3) of Unregulated Deposit Scheme Banning Act 2019 and Section 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B, 406 of IPC.

The applicant is in custody since 23.04.2025.
2.
As per the prosecution story, the allegation against present applicant is that he alongwith co-accused persons committed fraud upon several persons on the pretext of doubling the money.

Therefore, offence has been registered against the present applicant under the aforesaid sections.
3.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He is in custody since 23.04.2025.
It is submitted that co-accused persons Surya Prakash Bhondekar, Nandkishor Maheshware, Ajay Kumar Tidke and Mahesh Tidke have been enlarged on bail by Coordinate Bench of this Court.
Present applicant has also granted bail in other cases by Coordinate Bench of this Court.
Charge sheet has been filed.
The NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:43040 2 MCRC-21790-2025 conclusion of the trial will take considerable time, therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the bail application and has prayed for it's rejection.
5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.

Consequently, bail application under Section 483 of B.N.S.S. for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands Hemraj Amadare vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34353021/
1 allowed.
6.

sentences.text: It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of B.N.S.S. 7 .
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
